\section{Limiting cases, pathologies, and falsifiable predictions}
\label{sec:edge-cases}

The following predictions are consequences of the common authority. They are
pre-validation statements, not reports of executed evidence. ``No output''
means no value carrying a calibrated SCI-CAL unit label; a diagnostic or
explicitly uncalibrated passthrough may exist only as a different product
state.

\small
\begin{longtable}{L{0.14\linewidth}L{0.25\linewidth}L{0.51\linewidth}}
\caption{Required limiting and pathological outcomes.}\label{tab:edge-cases}\\
\toprule
ID & Challenge & Falsifiable prediction \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
ID & Challenge & Falsifiable prediction \\
\midrule
\endhead

\Edge{001} & Zero opacity & For every supported array and finite admitted
airmass, \(\ell=0\), \(T=C=1\), and atmosphere correction changes neither
signal nor conditional uncertainty. With every other structural condition
satisfied, this may establish only \code{science-qualification-eligible}; it
does not establish an achieved \code{science-qualified} or
\code{calibrated-science} claim without the separately accepted evidence in
\Req{049}. \\

\Edge{002} & Increasing opacity & At fixed admitted \(X>0\), increasing
positive \(\tau_{225}\) strictly decreases \(T\) and increases \(C\) while
remaining finite. Any finite positive-opacity unity plateau is a failure. \\

\Edge{003} & Zenith and airmass & At zenith \(X=1\), \(\ell=\tau_{225}\).
At fixed positive opacity, a larger admitted airmass gives larger \(\ell\) and
larger correction. At zero opacity the result is independent of airmass. \\

\Edge{004} & Exact atmosphere node & Evaluation at \(\ell_{a,k}\) returns the
declared authoritative \(-\ln T^{\rm eff}\) ordinate exactly, followed by the
declared exponential orientation. Interpolation of transmission or correction
instead is detectable at nontrivial intervals. \\

\Edge{005} & Operator seam & Left and right values agree at every node. Slopes
may differ; a derivative or linear covariance claim exactly at, or spanning,
a seam is unavailable and requires nonlinear propagation. \\

\Edge{006} & Invalid operator domain & A value outside numeric node support,
outside the upstream airmass model, or outside declared time support yields no
calibrated output. Clamping, extrapolation, and a legacy fallback are
detectable failures. \\

\Edge{007} & Bracketed opacity series & A sample between two valid source
states is admissible only if the named source interpolation rule authorizes
that bracket and its gap. Its lineage resolves both endpoints, method, and
validity interval. \\

\Edge{008} & Unbracketed opacity series & A sample before the first state,
after the last state, across a disallowed gap, or covered by only one endpoint
is outside temporal support. It yields no calibrated output rather than an
endpoint hold or extrapolation. \\

\Edge{009} & Engineering opacity & Any unsplit segment containing
\(0.15<\tau_{225}\leq0.25\) may receive one observation-level
\code{engineering-only} class. Every numerically supported sample uses the
same calibration operator, while the class conveys no science-quality claim. \\

\Edge{010} & Outside or malformed opacity & Negative or non-finite opacity is
invalid. Opacity above 0.25 or absent opacity is outside supported
calibration for the affected sample. Neither case is silently clamped or
relabeled, but a momentary unsupported sample does not automatically
invalidate other supported samples in the observation. \\

\Edge{011} & Unity factor & Replacing one required factor value by numeric
unity leaves values unchanged only when unity is the intended value; the
factor role and application count remain present and auditable. \\

\Edge{012} & Omitted, duplicated, or inverted factor & For an isolated
nonzero factor \(f\), output ratios are exactly those in
Equation~\eqref{eq:factor-challenges}. Signal and uncertainty discrepancies
identify the challenged role. \\

\Edge{013} & Corrected-APT double application & With
\(F^{\rm sel}=P F^{\rm parent}\), applying \(P\) again changes the result by
\(P\) and violates application count. Using the parent without the embodied
event changes it by \(P^{-1}\). An unapproved, unidentified, or
out-of-domain child transformation yields no calibrated output even when its
numeric value is plausible. \\

\Edge{014} & Keyed row permutation & Arbitrarily permuting selected APT rows
while preserving row occurrence keys and the explicit keyed relation leaves
every output, validity state, and nuisance recipient invariant. \\

\Edge{015} & Ordered-row permutation & Permuting rows under an ordered-row
binding without supplying a new proof invalidates the binding. A newly proven
permutation may be admitted and then gives the keyed-equivalent result. \\

\Edge{016} & Network or column reorder & Reordering network containers or
sample columns while preserving acquisition keys and bindings leaves results
invariant after restoring occurrence order. Inferring identity from the new
position produces a detectable mismatch or failure. \\

\Edge{017} & Missing or duplicate key & A missing acquisition/APT key,
duplicate keyed candidate, inconsistent array/network constraint, or multiple
sample columns for one selected occurrence invalidates the affected declared
scope. No first-row or nearest-row choice is allowed. \\

\Edge{018} & Association disposition & A unique admitted match may calibrate.
Abstained, ambiguous, rejected, and missing associations produce no calibrated
value for the endpoint; aggregate matcher performance cannot convert one into
a match. The matcher cannot become the owner of source-factor meaning, and an
association without an exact selected-child artifact is incomplete. \\

\Edge{019} & Irrelevant design identity & Adding, removing, or changing a
design-ID match while measured occurrence endpoints, association, selected
APT values, and all other state remain fixed leaves the SCI-CAL result
unchanged. \\

\Edge{020} & Scalar conditional uncertainty & Multiplying signal by \(M\)
multiplies variance by \(M^2\) and divides inverse variance by \(M^2\),
including for a signed \(F^{\rm sel}\). Support and validity do not change. \\

\Edge{021} & Vector conditional covariance & For a dense positive-definite
input covariance, the output equals \(A C_xA^{\mathsf T}\), including all
off-diagonal signs and magnitudes. Replacing it with a diagonal is not the
same claim. \\

\Edge{022} & Unavailable uncertainty & Removing a conditional uncertainty
input leaves it unavailable, not zero. Removing any required nuisance entry
marks total calibrated uncertainty unavailable while a separately valid
signal may remain. \\

\Edge{023} & Common systematic and sample count & A shared fractional scale
term gives Equation~\eqref{eq:common-rank-one}. Repeating or averaging
identically affected samples does not reduce that fractional term as
\(N^{-1/2}\). \\

\Edge{024} & Nonlinear nuisance case & Large/asymmetric factor uncertainty,
uncertainty crossing an operator seam, or uncertain discrete association
causes first-order propagation to be withheld. Posterior sampling or a bounded
sensitivity calculation need not agree with a local linearization. \\

\Edge{025} & Unresolved point source & Under a unit-peak originating beam and
a realized response with \(\rho_L=1\), an unresolved source of flux density
\(S\) mJy has ideal peak \(S\ \mjybeam\). This is a response prediction, not
an integrated-flux or target-color-corrected spectral claim. The result
retains the declared per-array reference-spectrum convention until the
downstream scientist applies a target color correction. \\

\Edge{026} & Response-changing kernel & If a downstream kernel changes
\(\rho_L\) to \(r\), the unrenormalized ideal peak is \(rS\ \mjybeam\). A
literal peak claim requires recorded renormalization by \(r^{-1}\) and an
updated response basis. \\

\Edge{027} & Circularized beam & Replacing available elliptical axes by a
circular beam without an explicit rule is nonconformant. With a declared
circularization, the result is labeled approximate and does not erase the
originating ellipse. \\

\Edge{028} & Unsupported stream or target & A non-\code{xs} stream, or a
request for surface brightness, per-pixel flux, temperature, extended-source
calibration, or integrated photometry, yields an unsupported no-output state
without a calibrated v0.1 label. A stream that is not the dimensionless fitted
KID resonance-frequency change cannot acquire calibrated meaning merely from
the \code{xs} token. \\

\Edge{029} & Zero signal and additive convention & With an explicit
ordinary \(x^{xs}=0\), every finite multiplier gives \(y=0\): CAL creates no
additive offset. Any nonzero additive CAL term is a detectable violation; DC
and correlated-mode removal belong to downstream PTC. \\

\Edge{030} & Observation-order replay & Two observations with distinct source
and child APTs, associations/transformations, delivery records, atmosphere,
photometric/order states, owner-decision snapshots, and response identities
give identical per-observation results in either processing order. No state
or factor from one appears in the other's canonical lineage. \\

\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\normalsize

\subsection{Proposed evidence, separated by claim}
\label{sec:validation-evidence}

No scientific validation is executed by this authorship task. Evidence must
follow the realizable TolTEC calibration workflow; it must not invent an
arbitrary combinatorial matrix or minimum sample size.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{V\arabic*.},leftmargin=*]
\item \Term{Analytic structural fixtures.} Use small scalar and dense-vector
  cases to evaluate Equations~\eqref{eq:affine-input},
  \eqref{eq:piecewise-operator}, \eqref{eq:multiplier},
  \eqref{eq:conditional-covariance}, and \eqref{eq:variance-weight}; include
  every edge in Table~\ref{tab:edge-cases}. Exact identities and metadata are
  compared exactly; numeric tolerances are preregistered for the arithmetic
  precision and never absorb a semantic mismatch.

\item \Term{Metamorphic identity and lineage fixtures.} Permute keyed rows,
  sample columns, and network containers; vary irrelevant design identity;
  challenge missing/duplicate keys and every association disposition; process
  observations in both orders; and inject omitted, duplicated, and inverted
  factor instances. Expected invariants and ratios are fixed by
  Equations~\eqref{eq:once-only} and \eqref{eq:factor-challenges}.

\item \Term{Atmosphere structural fixtures.} Verify the content-bound
  operator's commit and digests, exact nodes, analytic zero
  anchor, positivity, strict direction, seam continuity, and support rejection
  without using observational data. This establishes structural correctness
  only.

\item \Term{Atmosphere representation report.} Compare the finite retained
  operator with its named higher-fidelity generating calculation on a dense,
  reproducible grid over the exact declared support, using the exact selected
  passband identity and a fully declared weighting convention. Report maximum
  and distributional error separately by array, opacity, and airmass. The
  prior one-percent value is a reporting benchmark, not an automatic
  pass/fail ceiling. Unknown passband uncertainty remains a limitation.

\item \Term{Beammap closure test.} Reduce calibrated Beammaps to source APTs,
  have \code{toltec_beammap} establish that they are scientifically acceptable,
  enter them into \code{apt_library}, use TolProj's ordinary matching machinery
  to associate each APT back to its generating Beammap, and reduce that Beammap
  through the ordinary science path. Report recovered/input flux ratios or
  residuals separately for each array. This establishes end-to-end numerical
  closure of APT--TolProj--CAL--downstream processing, not independent absolute
  calibration accuracy.

\item \Term{Associated-pointing transfer test.} Use TolProj to apply an
  accepted Beammap-derived APT to that Beammap's associated pointing
  observation and reduce it through the same ordinary science path. When the
  pointing source has an adequate independent ALMA, SMA, planet, or
  well-calibrated asteroid flux, this tests calibration transfer. Across the
  observations actually available, record observation and source/child APT
  identities, TolProj association, reference and recovered flux, array,
  atmosphere, flux ratio or residual, repeatability, absolute recovery, and
  observed condition dependence. The five-percent and five-to-ten-percent
  values are reporting benchmarks only. Final scientific acceptance is an
  owner decision based on the honestly reported evidence.
\end{enumerate}
